claims.text: The untreated refractory high-entropy alloy has extremely high strength.
The untreated refractory high-entropy alloy exhibits impact-induced energy release.
The untreated refractory high-entropy alloy has limited ductility.
The untreated refractory high-entropy alloy deforms nonuniformly.
Rapid thermomechanical processing can produce a dual-phase microstructure containing uniformly dispersed coherent nanoprecipitates and secondary phases.
A uniformly distributed network of coherent nanoprecipitates and secondary phases controls dislocation motion.
A uniformly distributed network of coherent nanoprecipitates and secondary phases controls strain distribution.
The dual-phase microstructure provides multiple deformable paths.
Coherent interfaces impede localized strain accumulation.
The engineered microstructure enhances uniform plasticity.
The engineered microstructure preserves ultrahigh strength.
The engineered microstructure preserves impact-induced energy release.
Relative to the untreated alloy, the processed alloy will exhibit increased ductility during high-strain-rate impacts.
Relative to the untreated alloy, the processed alloy will exhibit more uniform deformation during high-strain-rate impacts.
The processed alloy will retain strength comparable to that of the untreated control.
The processed alloy will retain impact-induced energy release comparable to that of the untreated control.
The predicted benefits require successful formation of a uniformly dispersed, coherent nanoprecipitate network.
Compromised precipitate dispersion or interface integrity may prevent the predicted benefits.
Suitable rapid thermomechanical processing parameters are available in existing manufacturing setups.
